summary: Chat handshake and first-token stall after compiler runtime handoff during model upgrade
description: Issue summary: After a staged runtime/compiler handoff that accompanied a model variant upgrade, the customer reported sustained increases in Time-To-First-Token (TTFB) for chat completions. Impact: Several production chat flows for Arcadia Health experienced 5–10s delays for the first token; downstream UX times out on some clients. Environment: prod-us-east serving clustered behind API gateway, dedicated enterprise account with model pin to redwood-chat-v1. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send multi-turn chat request using model redwood-chat-v1 pinned to customer account. 2) Observe streaming connection establishes but first token delayed 3–10s. 3) Reproduce intermittently (~20% of requests during peak). Logs and traces: initial connection completes, but backend shows stall during kernel selection and KV cache warming. Error rates: no 5xx spike; elevated 500ms+ cold-prefetch tasks and some handshake retries at application layer. Workaround attempted: Customer temporarily pinned to runtime v1.8.4, observed restored TTFB back to baseline. Customer impact: production chat UIs for clinicians experiencing degraded interactivity; support request escalated by CSM.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Routing policy change caused increased routing to recently upgraded nodes that require kernel re-initialization and KV cache warmup.
Hypothesis 2: Compiler runtime update introduced a regression in the quantized kernel warmup path, causing extra synchronous work before first token emission.
Evidence: Traces show a spike in kernel-selection latency (0.8s -> 1.6s) and increased scheduler queue wait for prefetch tasks. No increase in 5xx or memory pressure on the nodes.
Reproduced internally by replaying production traces against a canary cluster with runtime 1.9.1 and observed 25% of connections showing 2–6s stall before first token unless warm pool present.
Mitigation test: Force warm pool (keepalive / prewarmed sessions) eliminated the stall, indicating cache/warmup as the primary factor.
Related change: PR runtime/pull/4123 updated node-selection heuristics and kernel init ordering; revert of selection heuristics reduced routing to cold nodes by ~90% in canary tests.

Action items: 1) Revert selection heuristic change in 1.9.2; 2) Add asynchronous kernel warmup to reduce blocking in token path; 3) Add telemetry to track per-node cold-session ratio and first-token latency percentile per model.
Cross-references: linked INT-4021 for internal tracking of runtime rollback and SUP-24193 for a prior similar TTFB pattern following a model/runtime sync event.
resolution: Root cause: Twofold — (A) a node-selection heuristic change caused more traffic to be routed to freshly upgraded nodes without warm pools; (B) a regression in the quantized kernel warmup path made first-token emission block on synchronous initialization. Remediation: Rolled back the node-selection heuristic for the customer and rolled out runtime patch 1.9.2 that defers kernel initialization and introduces async warmup/priming. Customer-facing fix: Arcadia Health pinned to v1.8.4 during mitigation window; patch deployed globally in 1.9.2 and verified. Follow-ups: implement telemetry dashboards for cold-session amplification and add an automated warm-pool policy for enterprise accounts during rollouts. Resolution verified: 2026-03-14 by observing 99th percentile TTFB return to baseline and customer confirmation.
